newsitem.title: POLAND: India's Sharma, tired, cancels event in Poland.
newsitem.headline: India's Sharma, tired, cancels event in Poland.

text.p: Indian President Shankar Dayal Sharma cancelled an event during his visit to Poland on Tuesday in order to rest for a while, PAP news agency reported.
It said Sharma, 78, in Krakow on the second and final day of his trip, dropped a scheduled tour of part of the southern city's Jagiellonian University and went to a hotel.
"The reason for the decision was his tiredness," Krakow city spokesman Maciej Bobr told the agency.
Sharma's wife dropped a planned walkabout on Krakow's main square in order to be with her husband, and merely stopped there briefly.
The Indian president later visited Krakow's royal castle and attended a lunch in a city restaurant.
He was then scheduled to visit the former Nazi German death camp of Auschwitz to pay tribute to up to 1.5 million people, mostly Jews, murdered there during World War Two.

On Monday Sharma, leading a 130-strong delegation of politicians and business executives, witnessed the signing in Warsaw of bilateral agreements on mutual protection of investment, cultural and scientific exchanges and joint efforts to combat organised crime.

His trip was partly designed to stimulate Polish-Indian trade, which tumbled after the fall of communism, when the two countries abandoned barter exchanges. It began to grow in 1992 and reached $186 million last year compared to $129 million in 1994.
